crm_notes:
Summary: Orbit Fallback Solutions is a contact-center tech operator focused on reducing live-AGENT load across large telco and ecommerce clients. They ingest ~800M chat turns/month (peak spikes + seasonal). Main ask: cost-sensitive, reliable deflection and agent-assist with fast p95 and graceful degradation under spikes.

Customer quotes/voice: "If we can't keep unit cost under $0.004/token-equivalent at our 90th percentile load, we won't greenlight dedicated capacity."

Technical requirements / priorities (shorthand):
- Workloads: high-volume chat deflection (primary), agent-assist (secondary), ticket summarization, tool-calling for CRM ops.
- Targets: deflection >= 40% on pilot topics; p95 assist latency < 500ms; tail latency handling for spikes; SLA for fallbacks.
- Cost sensitivity: heavy - wants hard cap for token-equivalent unit economics; exploring batching + prefix KV caching + int8 quantization to reduce per-token cost.
- Model preferences: open to Llama-2-derivatives, prefers Redwood-verified quantized stacks; wants model variants for routing (high-accuracy vs low-cost).
- Routing: needs smart routing policy (latency-first for VIP flows, cost-first for bulk deflection), automatic fallback to smaller model under capacity constraints.
- Observability: requires token-level cost breakdown, call traces for tool-calls, and per-route rollback capability.

POC notes:
- We loaded 10K sample conversations; initial batching improved throughput but increased p95 by ~40ms.
- KV/prefix caching reduced repeated prompt tokens by ~18% in the ticket-summary test.
- int8 quantized model cut inference cost estimate ~35% but customer flagged hallucination/format drift on structured tool-calls. SE assigned to run focused evaluation on tool-calling fidelity with quantized kernels.

Sales posture: mid-market ARR potential but runway to enterprise if residency + SLA + predictable unit economics validated.

Next steps (explicit):
1) SE to deliver quantized fidelity report and unit-econ model (due 2026-03-10).
2) Pricing team to propose capped-burst package for Q3 spikes.
3) Legal to clear data residency/retention clauses.
